import { SandboxLoginTable, SandboxCompare, SandboxRepositories } from '@site/src/components/Sandboxes';

Try out a fully set up Infrahub instance in your browser. Each sandbox has the data and automation for one type of network already loaded, so you can work through a complete change, from request to merge:

- Make the change, such as adding a rack to an AI data center fabric, or requesting a new data center or a customer VPN
- View the IP addresses, interfaces and device configurations that Infrahub generates for it
- Review the change in a Proposed Change, Infrahub's equivalent of a pull request, and merge it

Sandboxes are reset every night, so the changes you make are removed.

## When to start with a sandbox

Start with a sandbox to:

- Evaluate whether Infrahub fits your team's automation work
- Try Infrahub from a laptop or phone where you cannot install software

To check how Infrahub models your own data, performs at your scale or connects to your systems, [run Infrahub on your own machine](#run-infrahub-on-your-own-machine).

## Run Infrahub on your own machine

Run a demo on your own machine to adapt it to your network: change its schema, data and Generators, and keep your changes for as long as you need them.

For each demo, clone its GitHub project, start Infrahub in Docker and load the demo's data, as its guide describes:

Model your own network: [install Infrahub](/overview/quickstart), then begin with a schema from the [Infrahub Marketplace](/schema/marketplace), or describe your network to an AI assistant and have it build the schema, as [Build with AI](/overview/build-with-ai) describes.
